# Gāthāsaṅgaṇika (Pvr 10)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Gāthāsaṅgaṇika* ("Verses on the training rules") is the tenth chapter of the *Parivāra*, the final book of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It presents an interrogation and exposition of monastic discipline and Vinaya topics formatted as an exchange of verses [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral]. The text and its versified rulings—including a section referred to in commentary as the *Dutiya-gāthā-saṅgaṇika*—are treated in the Vinaya exegetical tradition, such as the *Samantapāsādikā* (preserved in Chinese translation as the *Shan-Chien-P'i-P'o-Sha*), where commentators expound verses concerning dawn rising in relation to offences such as *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* and *Saṅghādisesa* [Bapat and Hirakawa 1970].
SuttaCentral notes curated passage-level parallels between verses of the *Gāthāsaṅgaṇika* and the *Nirvāṇavarga* of Sanskrit and Chinese Dharmapada/Udānavarga traditions (UV 26, UVS 26, Uv Kg 26, T 210.36, T 212.27, and T 213.26) [SuttaCentral]. Related verses or references also appear across Pali texts such as the *Udāna* (Ud 5.5), *Theragāthā* (Thag 6.13), the *Khandhaka* (Kd 19), *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37), and *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2) [SuttaCentral]. In DharmaNexus machine alignments, the text shares 232 matching passages across 23 Pali works, demonstrating extensive textual overlap with Vinaya treatises and commentaries, particularly the *Vinayavinicchaya* and its *ṭīkā*, the *Parivāra-aṭṭhakathā*, other *Parivāra* sections (such as *Antarapeyyāla*, *Katāpattivāra*, and *Katthapaññattivāra*), and the *Visuddhimagga* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects cross-language alignments with Sanskrit Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya texts (such as the *Poṣadhavastu*, *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya*, and *Adhikaraṇavastu*) and Tibetan canonical Vinaya materials [DharmaNexus].
